incidents.name: Elevated Error Rates for Cloud Routers and Studio UI

incident_updates.body:
We are marking this incident resolved on the Apollo side.

For any continuing matters, please consult our support portal: https://support.apollographql.com/

The upstream provider has indicated recovery on their status page (https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/8gmgl950y3h7).

At the same time, we have seen our own monitors return to non-triggered states.  We will continue to monitor for the next 15 minutes and then declare this Resolved.

While Cloud Routers were impacted throughout the incident, the Studio UI impact was during two distinct periods: Nov 18 11:52 am – Nov 18, 12:10 pm UTC (18 minutes) and again from Nov 18, 12:51 pm – Nov 18, 1:09 pm UTC (another 18 minutes).  Studio UI was otherwise available in times outside of that range.

At this time, our monitors indicate that only Cloud Routers hosted on Apollo infrastructure are impacted as a result of an upstream service provider incident.

Studio UI has already recovered. Beyond these two impacted services, there has been no impact to APIs (including Uplink).
We're continuing the monitor the affected services while the upstream provider remediates the issue.

Our DNS provider has provided an update:

"The issue has been identified and a fix is being implemented."

We will be monitoring for recovery of our systems.
We're experiencing elevates error rates due to an upstream DNS provider major incident.

incidents.name: AWS us-east-1 Outage Impacting Apollo Services

incident_updates.body:
We will mark this as resolved as issues impacting our service have been resolved either through mitigation or upstream provider resolution. While some of our dependent services have indicated there is on-going stabilization of their own systems (following on the AWS us-east-1 disruptions yesterday) any unresolved items have NO impact to our offerings.  In the event that we have new findings or degradations, we will open a new incident.

Thank you for your patience while we adapted toward changing circumstances following on yesterday's events, and thank you to teams across the industry who worked (or may still be working) tirelessly toward recovery.
Systems remain stable and operational on our side, though we are still monitoring dependent software closely before we mark this resolved.  We will post another update within 60 minutes.
All systems appear operational but some of our 3rd party dependencies have not fully recovered.  Will continue to monitor.
We are continuing to monitor for any further issues.
We are continuing to monitor for any further issues.

Apollo Products hosted in AWS may be running into performance issues as problems at the Cloud Hosting Provider are remediated. 

Please use the "contact support" button in Studio if you require further bespoke assistance from Apollo.

AWS has reported continued degradation after initial signs of recovery. We are seeing some minor impacts to the AWS Uplink service, which we are continuing to monitor.

As we've previously stated we recommend customers to allowlist AWS and GCP Uplink endpoints which Apollo provides. Allowlisting both endpoints will allow seamless fallback if one is having issues. We have not seen any impact to GCP Uplink. 

Thanks for your patience during the matter and thank you for the AWS teams working toward full recovery.

incidents.name: AWS us-east-1 Outage Impacting Multiple Apollo Services

incident_updates.body:
As a result of the AWS us-east-1 system recovery, our own systems have also recovered, including AWS Uplink and AWS-hosted Cloud Routers.  At this time we will mark this issue as Resolved, though we will continue to monitor for any possible reoccurrence.

As noted in a previous update, the default configuration for Apollo Router and Apollo Gateway deployments is to roam between Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Amazon Web Services (AWS) endpoints in the event that one or the other is available.  If you have changed your configuration to rely on merely one provider, we recommend considering a configuration with fallback redundancy.  Please contact support if you need assistance with this configuration.

Additionally, our support systems have recovered and we believe any issues opened during the AWS incident have been received by our support teams.  If you believe your issue has not been received, please feel free to reach out to our support team again.

AWS is reporting signs of recovery on their status page and we are seeing recovery in several of our triggered monitors for systems which rely on AWS, however, we continue to monitor the overall situation as AWS processes a backlog of events in us-east-1.

As noted in the previous update, on-premise/self-hosted routers would only be impacted if their default configuration to roam between AWS and GCP has been changed to only rely on AWS. 

Anecdotally, we are seeing various non-Apollo systems regain previously unavailable functionality.

AWS has suggested additional updates will occur within the next 30 minutes and we will update our own system statuses when we are confident they are fully recovered.

Thanks for your patience during the matter and thank you for the AWS teams working toward full recovery.

Outage in AWS us-east-1 is impacting multiple Apollo products including Uplink (AWS), Cloud Routers and customer's ability to open supports tickets. 

By default Routers are configured to use GCP and AWS for Uplink, however if you have configured your router to use AWS exclusively there may be delays in schema updates, persisted queries manifests or the ability to bring new routers online, until the AWS outage is resolved.

AWS Outage Link: https://health.aws.amazon.com/health/status

incidents.name: GitHub CDN issues causing Rover, MCP, Router installer to serve 404 or stale artifacts

incident_updates.body: This incident has been resolved.

We have received confirmation from our upstream vendor that they have identified the errant code on their end, and have seen their alerts resolve.

We will be closing this at this time, please feel free to reach out to support, or to Apollo on our open source GH Issues.

Thanks as always for your patience!
We are seeing recovery and our alerts have returned to normal.  We did see that this originally started at 2025-08-08 04:27 UTC, and we will need to backdate it.

We have identified that GitHub's CDN is returning 404s or stale data for Apollo release artifacts.  We rely on the GitHub CDN for serving our release artifacts for tools which are distributed on GitHub, including Rover, the Apollo MCP Server and Router.

At this time, GitHub does not have a public status page that shows this, but there are many reports of it on the GitHub Community forums and there is correspondence on other projects (such as the Aqua project, seen here: https://github.com/aquaproj/aqua/issues/4068#issuecomment-3166806915). 

We are seeing early signs of recovery.
